edit_from_base: 'to the player's collision mask' -> 'to the player's collision layer'
prompt: Players fall through the platforms. Fix it by putting the platforms on collision layer 2 and adding layer 2 to the player's collision layer, with movement done in _physics_process.

config.plan_model: Agent-tool model parameter 'sonnet' (Claude Code sub-agent; the harness did not report the resolved model id)
config.how: one fresh general-purpose sub-agent per plan, reads a job file with project brief + the developer prompt, writes numbered plan (<=8 steps, no code) via Write; not Claude Code plan mode

plans.text:
1. Open level_01.tscn and the TileMapLayer node to confirm how the platforms are currently set up and which collision layer and mask they use.
2. In the TileMapLayer's TileSet, check that the platform tiles actually have physics shapes defined, since missing shapes are a common cause of falling through.
3. Set the platform TileMapLayer's collision layer to layer 2 only, leaving ground on its existing layer unless it should change too.
4. Select the Player's CharacterBody2D and add layer 2 to its collision layer, keeping its existing layers intact.
5. Check the Player's collision mask so it includes the layer the platforms now sit on (layer 2), since the mask is what makes the player detect them.
6. Open player.gd and make sure all movement and move_and_slide handling runs inside _physics_process rather than _process, moving it there if not.
7. Check that the two enemy scenes' layers and masks are not broken by the change, adjusting only if they need to interact with the platforms.
8. Run level_01.tscn and test that the player lands on and walks across the platforms, then confirm that jumping and enemy interaction still behave correctly.

1. Open level_01.tscn and the TileMapLayer's TileSet to confirm how the platforms are currently set up. Check that physics layers and collision shapes are actually defined on the platform tiles.
2. In the TileSet, set the platform tiles' physics layer to collision layer 2. Make sure each platform tile has a collision polygon painted in the TileSet's physics section.
3. Check the TileMapLayer node's own collision settings. Confirm collision is enabled and that its layer matches layer 2.
4. Select the Player's CharacterBody2D and add layer 2 to its collision layer, keeping its existing layers. Check that its collision mask includes layer 2 as well, since the mask is what makes the player detect the platforms.
5. Confirm the Player's CollisionShape2D has a shape assigned, is not disabled, and is sized to match the sprite.
6. Open player.gd and verify that all movement and gravity logic runs in _physics_process, not _process. Move any movement code there and use the physics delta.
7. Check that the movement uses the CharacterBody2D's built-in move-and-slide call and its floor handling, and that the enemy scenes' layers and masks do not conflict with the new layer 2.
8. Run level_01.tscn and test that the player lands on and walks across the platforms without falling through. Test again with the enemies present.

1. Open level_01.tscn and the TileMapLayer's TileSet, and note the current physics layer setup and each layer's collision layer and mask values. Confirm the tiles actually have collision shapes defined on the physics layer.
2. Set the platform TileMapLayer's collision layer to layer 2 (and the ground layer too, if the developer wants it consistent). Keep layer numbering consistent with the project's layer names in Project Settings.
3. Select the Player CharacterBody2D and add layer 2 to its collision layer, keeping its existing layer bit. Check that its collision mask includes layer 2, since the mask decides what it collides with and the layer alone will not stop the fall.
4. Open player.gd and find where gravity, velocity, and move_and_slide are handled. Verify all movement and physics code runs in _physics_process rather than _process.
5. Move any movement or gravity logic found in _process into _physics_process, using the physics delta, and leave input-only or visual logic where it is.
6. Check the Player's CollisionShape2D for a valid shape with a sensible size and position, and that the TileMapLayer's physics is enabled with collision turned on.
7. Review the two enemy scenes for collision layer and mask settings, and update their masks to include layer 2 so they do not fall through the platforms either.
8. Run level_01.tscn and test landing, walking, and jumping on platforms and ground. Confirm the player no longer falls through and that nothing else regressed.

1. Open level_01.tscn and the TileMapLayer's TileSet to inspect the current physics layer setup and confirm the platform tiles actually have collision shapes defined.
2. Set the TileSet's physics layer collision layer to 2 for the ground and platform tiles, and note the mask value so it does not conflict with other nodes.
3. Select the Player CharacterBody2D and add layer 2 to its collision layer, keeping any existing layers; also check that its collision mask includes layer 2 so it can detect the platforms.
4. Open player.gd and verify that all movement and gravity logic runs in _physics_process rather than _process, moving any misplaced logic there.
5. Confirm that move_and_slide is called once per physics frame and that velocity is applied in _physics_process only.
6. Check the two enemy scenes' collision layers and masks so the change does not make them fall through or collide unexpectedly with the platforms.
7. Run level_01.tscn and test that the player lands on, walks across, and jumps between platforms without falling through.
8. Verify the CollisionShape2D on the Player is sized correctly and the enemies still behave properly, then report the changes made.

1. Open level_01.tscn and the TileMapLayer's TileSet to confirm which physics layer the platform tiles currently use and whether the platform tiles actually have collision polygons painted on them.
2. Set the TileMapLayer's collision layer to layer 2 (and clear layer 1 for it if it is not needed for the ground), keeping the ground and platforms consistent with the request.
3. Open the Player's CollisionShape2D and CharacterBody2D settings and add layer 2 to the player's collision layer, as the developer asked, while leaving its existing layer and mask bits intact.
4. Check the player's collision mask and make sure it includes layer 2, since the mask (not the layer) is what determines what the player collides with and stands on; flag this to the developer if the requested change alone would not stop the falling.
5. Read player.gd and confirm all movement, gravity, and move_and_slide logic runs in _physics_process rather than _process, moving anything that is in the wrong callback.
6. Check the two enemy scenes for collision layer and mask settings so the layer 2 change does not make them fall through or collide unexpectedly with the platforms.
7. Run level_01.tscn and test walking, jumping, and landing on the platforms and ground, including one-way platform behavior if used.
8. Summarize the changes to the developer, noting any difference between what was requested and what was needed to actually fix the bug.

1. Open level_01.tscn and the TileMapLayer node, and confirm how the platforms are currently set up (which tiles are platforms, and whether the tileset has a physics layer with collision shapes defined).
2. In the TileSet resource, set the physics layer's collision layer to layer 2 for the platform tiles, so platforms live on layer 2 (and make sure the tiles actually have collision polygons).
3. Select the Player CharacterBody2D and update its collision layer to include layer 2 in addition to its existing layer, leaving other layers unchanged.
4. Check the player's collision mask: since the player must detect the platforms, confirm the mask includes layer 2 (the platform layer), as falling-through is usually a mask issue, and add it if missing.
5. Open player.gd and verify all movement, gravity, and move_and_slide logic runs in _physics_process; move anything currently in _process into _physics_process.
6. Check the two enemy scenes and any other bodies for collision layer/mask settings that might conflict with the new layer 2 assignment, and adjust if they also need to collide with platforms.
7. Verify the Player's CollisionShape2D is enabled, has a valid shape, and is correctly sized and positioned relative to the Sprite2D.
8. Run level_01.tscn and test that the player lands and walks on platforms, jumps onto them, and that enemies still behave correctly.

1. Open level_01.tscn and the TileMapLayer's TileSet to confirm how the platform tiles currently have physics shapes and which collision layer they sit on. Check whether the platform tiles actually have collision polygons defined, since missing shapes would also cause falling through.
2. In the TileSet's physics layer settings, set the platform tiles' collision layer to layer 2, as the developer requested. Leave the ground tiles on their existing layer unless they also need to change.
3. Open the Player's CharacterBody2D properties and add layer 2 to its collision layer, keeping its existing layer bits. Also check the player's collision mask, since the mask is what makes it detect the platforms.
4. Verify the player's collision mask includes layer 2, and add it if not. Note this to the developer, because the layer alone will not stop the fall without the mask.
5. Open player.gd and find where gravity and movement are applied, including any use of _process or _input for motion. Move all movement and move_and_slide logic into _physics_process so it runs on the physics tick.
6. Check that the CollisionShape2D on the Player has a valid shape and is not disabled, and that the enemy scenes' layers and masks do not clash with the new layer 2 setup.
7. Run level_01.tscn and test landing on, walking along, and jumping through the platforms, at several frame rates. Confirm the player no longer falls through.
8. Summarize the changes for the developer, flagging that the mask change and any collision-shape fixes went slightly beyond the literal request.

1. Open level_01.tscn and the TileMapLayer, and confirm how the platforms are currently set up: which tile set physics layer they use and what collision layer and mask values are in place.
2. Check player.gd and the Player node to see how movement is done now (for example, whether it runs in _process or _physics_process) and what the player's current collision layer and mask are.
3. In the TileSet resource, make sure the platform tiles actually have collision polygons on a physics layer, since missing polygons are a common cause of falling through.
4. Set the TileMapLayer's collision layer so the platforms live on layer 2, keeping ground on its existing layer unless the ground should move too.
5. On the Player CharacterBody2D, add layer 2 to the collision layer as requested, and make sure the collision mask includes layer 2 so the player actually detects the platforms.
6. Move all movement logic in player.gd (velocity handling, gravity, and the move-and-slide call) into _physics_process, so it runs on the physics tick.
7. Check the two enemy scenes and any other bodies for collision layer or mask conflicts caused by the change, and adjust their masks if they should also stand on layer 2.
8. Run level_01 and test that the player lands on and walks across the platforms, then confirm the enemies and ground still behave correctly.

1. Open level_01.tscn and the TileMapLayer's physics settings to confirm how the platforms are currently configured (collision enabled, physics layer defined in the tile set, shapes present on the platform tiles). This establishes the baseline before changing anything.
2. Check the tile set's physics layer and set that layer's collision layer to layer 2 so the platform tiles live on layer 2, adjusting the platform tiles' collision shapes if any are missing.
3. Open the Player's CollisionShape2D/CharacterBody2D properties and add layer 2 to the player's collision layer, keeping its existing layer and mask settings otherwise intact.
4. Verify the player's collision mask includes layer 2 as well, because a body only detects what is on layers in its mask; flag this to the developer, since the requested change to the layer alone may not stop the fall.
5. Review player.gd and confirm all movement, gravity, and move_and_slide logic runs in _physics_process rather than _process, moving any misplaced movement code there.
6. Check that the enemy scenes and any other bodies still collide with the ground and platforms correctly after the layer change, adjusting their masks only if they break.
7. Run level_01.tscn and test landing on, walking along, and jumping onto each platform and the ground to confirm the player no longer falls through.
8. Report back what was changed, including the mask caveat, and note anything that behaved differently from the requested approach.

1. Open level_01.tscn and the TileMapLayer node, and confirm how the platforms are currently configured (physics layer set on the tile set, which tiles have collision polygons). Also note the Player's current collision layer and mask values.
2. In the TileSet resource, make sure a physics layer exists and that the platform tiles have collision shapes painted on them, since missing shapes are a common cause of falling through.
3. Set the TileSet physics layer's collision layer to layer 2 (and leave ground on its existing layer unless it should also move), as the developer requested.
4. Select the Player CharacterBody2D and add layer 2 to its collision layer, keeping its existing layer bits intact.
5. Check the Player's collision mask includes layer 2 as well, because the mask is what actually makes the body detect and collide with the platforms; flag this to the developer since the requested change alone may not stop the falling.
6. Open player.gd and verify gravity and movement (velocity updates and move_and_slide) all run inside _physics_process rather than _process, moving them there if not.
7. Check the two enemy scenes and any other bodies for collision masks that should now include layer 2, adjusting only where they interact with platforms.
8. Run level_01.tscn, test landing on and walking across the platforms and jumping through edges, and report back what was changed along with the mask caveat.
